column3: Close to the Greek; “Son of God” is in the critical text, though some manuscripts lack it.
NASB follows the critical text with “in Isaiah the prophet” (Textus Receptus: “in the prophets”) and lacks “before you.”
Close to the Greek; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB has “John the Baptist,” following the critical text’s “the one baptizing”; “came” is rendered “appeared,” and “proclaiming” is “preaching.”
NASB adds “wore” and renders “eating” as “his diet was.”
NASB moves “after me” to the front; “strap” is rendered “thong.”
NASB follows the critical text with “out of” and “upon”; “tearing open” is rendered “opening.”
“Drives out” is rendered “impelled Him to go out.”
NASB follows the critical text with “the gospel of God” (Textus Receptus: “of the kingdom of God”); “delivering up” is rendered “taken into custody.”
“Has drawn near” is rendered “is at hand.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the brother of Simon”).
NASB has no “from there,” like the critical text; “adjusting” is rendered “mending,” and it adds “also.”
NASB has no “Ha!”, like the critical text; “What to us and to You” is rendered “What business do we have with each other.”
NASB follows the critical text: “A new teaching with authority!”
